title: Calcium Measurements in Mouse Primary Skeletal Muscle Fibers
author: Youhanna, Bruton, et al.

steps.title: Prepare incubation media
steps.instruction: Place 50 mL of complete DMEM/F12 in a 37 °C incubator.

steps.title: Prepare collagenase solution
steps.instruction: Prepare 5 mL of supplemented collagenase type I.

steps.title: Clean FDB muscles
steps.instruction: Remove tendons, connective tissue, and blood vessels from the flexor digitorum brevis (FDB) muscles.

steps.title: Enzymatic digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate the cleaned muscle in the supplemented collagenase for 2–3 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: Transfer to fresh media
steps.instruction: Move the muscles to 3 mL of fresh DMEM/F12 that was pre‑warmed in step 1.

steps.title: Gentle trituration
steps.instruction: Using a regular blue plastic 1 mL pipette tip filled with 900 µL DMEM/F12, pipette slowly up and down 10–20 times (≈1 s up, 1 s down) to separate individual fibers.

steps.title: Plate fiber suspension
steps.instruction: Transfer 300 µL of the resulting fiber suspension into laminin‑coated 35 mm glass‑bottom Petri dishes.

steps.title: Allow fiber attachment
steps.instruction: Incubate the dishes for 15 min at 37 °C to let fibers attach.

steps.title: Add culture medium
steps.instruction: Add 2.7 mL of supplemented DMEM/F12 to each dish. Fibers can be used for experiments up to 4 h after attachment.

steps.title: Set up dissection tray
steps.instruction: Place the FDB muscle in a custom dissection tray equipped with two hollow movable metal 10G syringe needles mounted at opposite ends.

steps.title: Fix tendons in needles
steps.instruction: Insert the proximal and distal tendons into the split ends of nylon rods located inside the 10G needles; pull the rods to hold the tendons tightly and rotate needles as needed.

steps.title: Expose muscle fibers
steps.instruction: Remove connective tissue, fat, and visible blood vessels with sharpened dissection forceps and scissors.

steps.title: Divide muscle into digits
steps.instruction: Longitudinally separate the FDB muscle into three digits, keeping some fibers of each digit attached to both tendons (proximal and distal). Use a stereomicroscope with dark‑field illumination up to 40× magnification.

steps.title: Mount a digit
steps.instruction: Mount one digit in the dissection tray and fix it into the split rods on both sides.

steps.title: Test electrical responsiveness
steps.instruction: Apply a single supramaximal electrical stimulus (≤10 V) with a pen‑type stimulator; a brief twitch of a few milliseconds followed by relaxation indicates intact fibers. Use a pen‑type electrode connected to a current pulse stimulator capable of up to 100 V (World Precision Instruments, model SYS‑A300 or Aurora Scientific, model 701C).

steps.title: Select twitching fibers
steps.instruction: At 40× magnification, identify twitching fibers on the FDB surface and isolate them by cutting away surrounding fibers in small steps, repeatedly checking for robust contraction and avoiding overstretching.

substeps.instruction: Check remaining fibers repeatedly for strong contraction.
Avoid damaging fibers by overstretching the digit.

steps.title: Isolate single fiber
steps.instruction: Choose one fiber and carefully remove all other fibers using jeweller’s forceps and micro‑iris scissors.

steps.title: Confirm isolated fiber function
steps.instruction: Stimulate the isolated single fiber electrically and verify that it contracts.

description: Methods used for cell isolation may result in alterations of the extracellular matrix (ECM), which can impact cellular functionality and affect experimental outcomes in a wide variety of tissues, including liver,2 lung,3 bone4 and skeletal muscle.5,6 In this protocol, we describe two simplified methods for the isolation of single primary skeletal muscle fibers: 1) enzymatic isolation; and 2) surgical microdissection. We then detail how to use those isolated fibers for calcium measurements. The microdissection method results in improved maintenance of mitochondrial functionality, calcium handling and cellular transcriptomes. The protocol constitutes an adaptation and amalgamation of several enzymatic and microdissection techniques described earlier.7,8,9
